criticalPath.explanation: The boundary bridge has the largest runtime/package join risk. Reader and typed-only qualification have disjoint paths and no native permission prerequisite. Integration joins source and inventory, not live success. It accepts an actionable negative typed-export result without pretending checkpoint equality works. Missing native approval still holds the original DevOps operation, not construction. No resume or E2E recheck is emitted on prospective source changes.
criticalPath.estimates: estimatedMinutes are rough implementation/review/integration scheduling estimates, never execution limits. Native/cloud duration is unknown.

governance.ownership: The first three tasks own only their disjoint listed paths. They do not edit the index, common integration tests, coverage document, canonical architecture, dependency manifests or each other's modules. Bridge supplies its optional sink/dispatch contract within its owned module before its internal wiring; reader consumes existing ScopeBinding/Manifest, not bridge implementation. No common foundation task is necessary.
governance.git: All task commits stay on the established feature branch in the shared checkout. Inspect staging and use git commit --only with explicit owned paths; ordinary transient index contention is retried without removing locks. Do not stage, stash, discard or commit another owner's work. Do not switch branches, force push or push moving HEAD. Disjoint source commits need no whole-assignment Git resource. Integration checks ancestry and records every task commit on the feature branch; any retained unmerged branch requires task/branch/commit IDs and abandonment reason in a feature-branch commit message, and the branch is kept.
governance.resources: Each initial task has its own scoped mutable resource and temporary fixture namespace. No shared index or Git resource serializes the initial fan-out. Use unique owned temp directories and no fixed ports/listeners. Integration exclusively owns repository-index refresh and full application/repository validation after accepted handoffs. Initial tasks run focused suites; integration runs the documented full checks once for the actual joined source and carries those results to original review. No concurrently running full checks, shared test state or package creation.
governance.integration: The explicit integration task reconciles the three accepted commits, updates index/package-closure fixtures and coverage only as necessary, and emits exact tested source bindings and limitations. This is construction integration, not the original formal E2E or DevOps stage. An essential selected-lab allowlist change not already covered must be evidenced and routed through existing Architect/Scrum scope, not silently added. No positive typed-export result is required to integrate the independently useful reader/bridge.
governance.checks: Use existing absolute Python and explicit selected-lab root from the authorized execution packet for Test-Demo.ps1, and scripts/Test-Repository.ps1. No dependency installation without manifest change or missing-tool failure. Affected retained checks are required only if retained tooling changes. Preserve baseline cases and report exclusions.
governance.preservation: Preserve accepted collection qualification 6e639517, exact-ref delivery de2deae/9b4919d8 and accepted unchanged-runtime E2E. No duplicate delivery, generic SDK inventory, new UI or re-review of accepted work. New source must earn its own affected verification. Preserve exactly three remote roles, deterministic gates, trusted binding, immutable outputs/exact refs, ETag publication, checkpoints, write-ahead holds and machine stdout. Historical rollback provenance stays WAIVED, never PASS.
governance.restrictions: No native denial retry or alternate route, credential acquisition, live create/send/stop/retrieval, cloud writes, publication, infrastructure/RBAC/network mutation, external upload, production profile, lossy checkpoint projection, SDK private patch or uncertain-effect replay. All sprints remain partial. Actual model-history provenance and live comparison gaps remain explicit.
